idiom_name: delegated properties backed by MutableMap<String, Any?> (by map)
implementation_notes: Kotlin replaces the trait interfaces with delegated properties: a class declares val model: String by doc and the standard library's getValue/setValue extensions on Map/MutableMap perform the lookup by property name, so the typed view is a language feature rather than hand-written cast-and-read accessors. The document is an ordinary MutableMap<String, Any?> (or a JSON tree), and children are nested maps that a small factory converts into child views, since the standard library has no children(key, constructor) helper. The map still carries no type information: a value stored under the wrong runtime type throws ClassCastException at the delegated getter, and a missing key throws NoSuchElementException rather than failing at compile time.
pitfalls: The key is the property name: rename the property or build the map with a different key and the first access throws NoSuchElementException instead of failing to compile.
Delegation casts but does not convert: a String stored under an Int-valued property throws ClassCastException, so untyped JSON needs a coercing delegate or a decoding step.
Only MutableMap delegation supports var properties - delegating a var to a read-only Map does not compile, and writes through the delegate are visible to every other holder of the same map.

variants.name: kotlinx.serialization JsonElement tree with serializable views
variants.implementation_notes: kotlinx.serialization provides both halves for JSON documents: JsonElement (JsonObject/JsonArray/JsonPrimitive) is the loosely typed tree, and the compiler plugin synthesises serializers for @Serializable data classes, which then act as typed views via Json.decodeFromJsonElement. The plugin and a matching kotlinx-serialization-json version are required; choose this over map delegation when the document's origin is JSON and the views should be real data classes rather than map-backed properties.
variants.code_sketch:
val doc = Json.parseToJsonElement(payload).jsonObject
val model = doc["model"]!!.jsonPrimitive.content   // loose access
@Serializable data class Car(val model: String, val price: Int)
val car = Json.decodeFromJsonElement<Car>(doc)      // typed view
val extra = doc["plugins"]                          // still reachable dynamically
pitfalls: JsonElement shape accessors (jsonObject/jsonPrimitive) throw on a wrong kind and indexing returns null, so the failure moves to the call site unless decodeFromJsonElement validates the whole tree.
@Serializable decoding ignores unknown keys by default, so a typo in a view property passes silently unless the Json instance is configured to be strict.
